title: After a restore, members who deleted their account in the last day come back, and nothing says to delete them again
what: The nightly copy keeps a member who deleted their account until it expires. The restore drill only checks that every row comes back identical. Neither the drill nor the written restore steps say to delete again the accounts that were deleted after the copy was taken, so a real restore quietly brings those members and their data back.
expected: The restore steps list the accounts deleted since the copy and delete them again, and a test or drill step checks that a member deleted after the copy is gone after the restore.
fix_line: Add a re-delete step to the restore guide and to the drill, using HQ's own record of deleted accounts

title: No test proves a failed member pop-up never undoes the gym's own approval, order change or report request
what: The pop-up notes are made inside the gym's own save (a pause approval, an order marked ready, a report request). The code turns any failure there into a warning, but no test makes the note fail and checks the gym's action still saved. No test checks that finished notes are later cleaned away either.
expected: A database test that forces the note step to fail and sees the approval, order and report request still saved, and one that sees old finished notes removed on a later run.
fix_line: Add two checks to the member pop-up database test: a failing note and the clean-up of old ones

title: Replying to a member's question in a paused gym, the 200-question list cap and the 180-day removal are never tested
what: The question test checks who sees a question, replies, taking back and leaving. It never tries a reply from a gym that is suspended, never fills the list past 200 or 60 days, and never ages a question past 180 days to see it removed.
expected: Database checks that a suspended gym's reply is refused SUSPENDED and not saved, that the list stops at 200 recent questions, and that a question older than 180 days is gone.
fix_line: Add the three missing checks to the ask-a-trainer database test

title: The trainer-question journeys promise short surnames and owner-cannot-read, but the phone test for the newer page shows full names and says the owner reads it too
what: The server journeys and the older database test say a member sees 'Rohit S.' and that a question sent to one trainer is hidden from the owner. The phone test for the newer 'Message your gym' page taps 'Vikram Rao' and 'Tara Singh (your trainer)' and checks the line 'The owner of the gym can read it too.' So the tests guard two different privacy promises and nobody checks which one members are told.
expected: One agreed rule for names and for whether the owner reads a trainer's question, written into the journeys and checked by both the database and the phone tests.
fix_line: Update the old journeys and test to the newer rule, or retire the old ask path

title: A member who left, or changed their check-in number, is never tested against the gym's payment requests
what: The payment-identity test checks matching, shared numbers, another gym and a dead key. It never makes a member leave and checks the gym's payment requests stop, and never changes a member's check-in number to see the requests stop until it matches again.
expected: Database checks that a member who left is refused and gets no request, and that a changed number gives no place on the list until it matches.
fix_line: Add a left member and a changed number to the payment-identity database test
